title: Incident learning catalog and action cadence
author: Mariana Ortiz
body:
Overview:

This document defines the Incident Learning Catalog (ILC), a lightweight process for turning incident evidence into prioritized, tracked improvements across runbooks, on-call policies, and product/infra changes. The ILC complements existing runbooks and postmortem frameworks by focusing on short feedback loops, measurable actions, and monthly synthesis cycles.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Close the loop between incidents and durable operational improvements with a predictable cadence and clear ownership.
- Scope: All Sev 1/2 incidents, customer-visible degradations, recurring SLO regressions, and game-day findings. Not intended for single-user support tickets.

Definitions:
- Incident Learning Catalog (ILC): central index of actions, experiments, and runbook edits derived from incidents and drills.
- Synthesis Cycle: monthly meeting to triage and prioritize ILC items into execution tranches.
- Action Item (AI): a discrete, timeboxed change with an owner and acceptance criteria.

Roles & responsibilities:
1) Incident Commander (IC): leads evidence collection and initial AI suggestions within 48 hours post-incident.
2) Owner (action owner): engineering or product team assigned to deliver a specific AI.
3) Synthesis Lead (ops-program): facilitates monthly synthesis cycle, reconciles duplicates, and ensures tracking hygiene.
4) Runbook Steward: maintains runbook edits derived from AIs and coordinates publishing.
5) Customer Success Liaison: validates comm templates and customer-facing AIs for enterprise-impacting incidents.

Incident lifecycle with ILC integration (step-by-step):
1. Contain & stabilize (0-2 hours): use service-specific runbook. IC opens a short incident summary in the incidents tracker and marks potential AIs inline.
2. Evidence capture (0-24 hours): collect metrics, traced spans, relevant logs, and sample requests. Attach artifacts to the incident page (links to traces, Grafana dashboards, request samples).
3. Immediate mitigations (0-48 hours): implement short-term mitigations and owner documents temporary fixes with rollback criteria.
4. Preliminary AI list (48-72 hours): IC publishes a preliminary AI list on the incident page following the AI template below. AIs should be small, testable, and labeled by priority and type (runbook, infra, product, monitoring).
5. Final post-incident package (within 10 business days): full timeline, RCA, and proposed AIs; mark items that must enter the next Synthesis Cycle.
6. Synthesis Cycle (monthly): Synthesis Lead runs a 60-minute triage to de-duplicate, score, and assign AIs to 30/60/90-day buckets.
7. Execution & verification: Owners implement AIs, link commits and PRs to the ILC item, and provide verification steps or KPIs.
8. Close & archive: after verification, the Synthesis Lead closes items and updates runbooks. Closed items are included in quarterly reliability metrics.

AI template (use on every incident page):
- AI title: short descriptive phrase
- Type: runbook | infra | monitoring | product | docs | process
- Priority: P0 | P1 | P2 (P0 = customer/system-critical)
- Owner: @username/team
- Due: YYYY-MM-DD
- Acceptance criteria: bullet list of measurable outcomes (e.g., canary passes, SLO delta < X%)
- Artifacts/links: PRs, dashboards, runbook pages

Triage & scoring rubric (used in Synthesis Cycle):
- Customer impact (0-5): how many customers affected and revenue risk
- Recurrence risk (0-5): probability of reoccurrence without change
- Visibility & debugging cost (0-5): time-to-detect / time-to-triage improvement
- Implementation cost (0-5): engineering work estimate (lower score = cheaper)
Total score = (Customer impact * 2) + Recurrence risk + Visibility cost - Implementation cost adjustment.
Note: use the spreadsheet template linked in the related pages for automated scoring.

Runbook edit & publishing workflow:
1. Create branch with runbook edits in the docs repo: docs/oncall/runbooks/<service>-<short-topic>.md
2. Link PR to ILC item and incident page.
3. Runbook Steward reviews for clarity and operational steps; run the checklist below.
4. Merge and publish: update runbook metadata (owner, last_tested, test_notes).

Runbook checklist (must be validated during synthesis or game day):
- Clear trigger conditions (metrics/traces)
- Step-by-step containment steps (commands and expected outcomes)
- Communication template snippets (bridge/SL/CS) included
- Rollback/undo instructions and safety guards
- Post-incident AI anchor (link to ILC item)

Game day integration and playbook tests:
- Frequency: each service should be exercised at least once per quarter or when a high-risk change lands.
- Objectives: validate detection, escalation, and containment steps; verify telemetry and dashboards; rehearse customer comms.
- Quick game-day script (60 minutes):
  1) 0-10m — inject signal and confirm alerting (SRE lead)
  2) 10-25m — IC declared, containment steps attempted (service owner)
  3) 25-40m — monitoring/observability gaps noted (observability lead records)
  4) 40-55m — customer comm draft and validation (CS liaison)
  5) 55-60m — debrief and immediate AIs captured into ILC (Synthesis Lead)

Status page and customer comm templates (examples)
- Status page short: "We are investigating elevated error rates for the Redwood text-inference service in us-west-2. Engineers have identified a degraded dependency and are working on mitigation. We'll update by 30 minutes or sooner."
- Internal bridge opener (first 15 minutes):
  Subject: [Incident] <service> increased error rate — IC opens bridge
  Body: Service, observed symptom, first detection time, impact summary, primary contact, current mitigation attempt.
- Customer update template (every 30–60 minutes while active):
  Subject: Redwood status update — <service> degradation in <region>
  Body: Short summary, actions taken, customer impact, ETA for next update, link to status page and support contact.

Example status page API (curl sample):
#!/bin/bash
# mark status as investigating via internal status API
curl -X POST https://status.redwood.internal/api/v1/events 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"service":"text-inference-usw2","status":"investigating","summary":"Elevated 5xx errors","started_at":"2026-02-15T14:12:00Z"}'

Post-incident verification & KPIs:
- Each closed AI must include a verification step: e.g., "error rate reduced to baseline for two weeks", "canary passes at 250 qps for 72 hours".
- Quarterly metrics collected by Synthesis Lead: number of AIs opened/closed, median time-to-close, percent of AIs causing runbook edits, and mean recurrence interval for same root cause class.

Escalation ladders and time targets (guiding targets):
- Acknowledgement target: 5 minutes for Sev1, 15 minutes for Sev2
- Incident commander declared: within 15 minutes for Sev1, within 1 hour for Sev2
- Preliminary AI list: within 72 hours
- Final post-incident package: within 10 business days

Maintenance & governance:
- Synthesis Lead conducts quarterly audit of ILC hygiene: stale items (>180 days) are either closed or re-scoped.
- Runbook Steward maintains a published test matrix showing last game-day or real-incident validation date per runbook.
- Additions or edits to the ILC require: link to incident/game-day, owner, due date, and at least one acceptance criteria.
